implementation_notes: Jest (and Vitest) implement the entire loop: toMatchSnapshot writes a pretty-printed reference under __snapshots__/ next to the test, later runs compare against it, -u/--updateSnapshot re-records, --ci makes the runner refuse to write and fail on mismatches, and obsolete snapshot entries are reported so the corpus does not rot. That replaces the hand-written recorder/comparator; the standard form is still justified for legacy subjects whose output only exists as an external artefact (CLI stdout, produced files), where you capture the process output into a string and snapshot that.
pitfalls: Blanket re-recording: jest -u rewrites every failing snapshot in one run; restrict re-recording with --testNamePattern or the watch-mode interactive review so the diff stays reviewable.
Snapshots capture more than intended (Dates, random ids, machine paths); scrub them with property matchers such as expect.any(Date) or a custom serializer.
Snapshot writes need a writable working tree, and CI must run with --ci so a pipeline cannot commit new baselines.
Inline vs external is a workflow decision: keeping every value in .snap files makes small assertions hard to read, so reserve toMatchInlineSnapshot for compact values.

variants.name: Inline snapshots written back into the test source
variants.implementation_notes: The inline realization keeps the reference inside the test file: toMatchInlineSnapshot() with no argument records the value into the call on the next run (prettier is used for formatting when present), and re-approval rewrites that literal. It is the better choice for small, stable values because the expectation is read in place, in the same diff as the code change; for multi-line artefacts the escaping and file churn are worse than a .snap file, so use the external variant there.
pitfalls: Inline snapshots rewrite source files, so runs must not execute in a read-only checkout (CI) with the update behaviour enabled.
Long multi-line values inside the source are awkward to review and can hit editor/prettier formatting churn; move them to a .snap file.
